## DECISION

*Fair Work Act 2009*  
s.185 - Enterprise agreement

# Super Retail Group Limited

# (AG2024/952)

# SUPER RETAIL GROUP RETAIL & CCC ENTERPRISE AGREEMENT 2024

Retail industry

DEPUTY PRESIDENT SLEVIN

SYDNEY, 2 MAY 2024

*Application for approval of the Super Retail Group Retail & CCC Enterprise Agreement 2024*

**[1]** An application has been made for approval of an enterprise agreement known as the 
*Super Retail Group Retail & CCC Enterprise Agreement 2024* (the Agreement). The 
application was made pursuant to s.185 of the *Fair Work Act 2009* (the Act) by Super Retail 
Group Limited. The Agreement is a single enterprise agreement. If the Commission is satisfied 
that the requirements in sections 186 and 187 of the Act are met it must approve the Agreement.

**[2]** Section 186(2)(c) requires the Commission to be satisfied that the agreement does not 
contravene s.55 relating to the interaction between the National Employment Standards (NES) 
and enterprise agreements. A concern was raised that the Agreement does not define a 
shiftworker for the purposes of the extra week of annual leave provided for in the NES (see 
s.187(4) and s.196 of the Act). In response the Applicant provided an undertaking that defines 
for the purpose of the NES a shiftworker to be an employee who is regularly rostered to work 
on Sundays and public holidays in a business in which shifts are continuously rostered 24 hours 
a day for 7 days a week.

**[3]** A further concern was raised in respect of clause 136 which provides for the 
circumstances where the employer is entitled to withhold an amount from an employee’s final 
payment upon termination. Clause 136 does not appear to limit the source of monies which may 
be deducted which may operate in a manner contrary to an employee’s entitlement to payment 
of NES entitlements upon termination. In response the Applicant provided an undertaking to 
amend clause 136 to reflect the limitation that wages for the period of no more than one week 
may be withheld, and only if the employee is agreed 18 years or older. This reflects an award 
standard which is otherwise permitted by the NES.

**[4]** Section 186(2)(d) requires the Commission to be satisfied the agreement passes the 
better off overall test (BOOT). The test is found in s.193 of the Act and it is to be applied in 
accordance with s.193A. Under s.193 the Commission must be satisfied, as at the time the 
application for approval was made, that each award covered employee, and each reasonably foreseeable employee, for the agreement would be better off overall if the agreement applied to 
the employee than the relevant modern award. Here the relevant awards are the *Clerks – Private 
Sector Award* (Clerks Award) and *General Retail Industry Award* (GRIA). In applying the test, 
the Commission is required by s.193A to make a global assessment of whether each employee 
would be better off having regard to the terms of the agreement which would be more beneficial 
than the Awards and the terms which would be less beneficial. In making that assessment, the 
Commission may have regard to the patterns or kinds of work, or types of employment, that are 
reasonably foreseeable at the time of the application.

**[5]** In this matter concerns were raised with the Applicant that various terms in the 
Agreement could be less beneficial depending on the patterns or kinds of work, or types of 
employment, applying at the workplace. In respect to rates of pay, a concern was raised that 
GRIA Level 4 classification employees who are 19 years old and younger may not be better off 
overall under the Agreement. In response the Applicant provided an undertaking that an updated 
Appendix A sets out revised rates for junior team members who are working at a GRIA Level 
4 classification by undertaking higher duties.

**[6]** Clarity was sought as to the correct classification matching adopted by the Applicant 
for the Shift Supervisor / GRIA Level 4 classification with the classification in the Award to 
assess whether the rates of pay might fall below Award rates. In response the Applicant 
indicated that the rates of pay at clause 305 of the Agreement relating to duties at Award Level 
4 is applicable to team members acting above a shift supervisor function in a Higher Duties 
arrangement as set out at clause 267. The Applicant clarified that the use of “Higher duties for 
a Supervisor / Shift Supervisor – GRIA Retail Employee Level 3” is an extension of terms for 
classifications at clause 251. The Applicant said employees’ wages should be mapped to a level 
4 GRIA (second-level manager) for periods no greater than 12 weeks, typically for coaching 
purposes and/or covering leave of the appointed second-level manager. Team members remain 
covered by the enterprise agreement as their substantive and ongoing role remains unchanged. 
The ordinary hours rate provided under clause 305 exceed GRIA ordinary hours rates by 11%. 
The Applicant further indicated that the application of junior rates to GRIA level 4 is not 
permitted and the impact this creates regarding a junior rate for clause 305. The Applicant 
provided a commitment to applying “at 20 years” / adult rates for any team member engaged in 
the position.

**[7]** Further concerns were raised in relation the Agreement appearing to be silent on a 
number of safeguards for part time employees which are provided for in both the Clerks and 
Retail Awards and whether these deficiencies may result in financial and non-financial 
detriment. As to the safeguard pertaining to reasonably predictable hours of work, provided for 
at clause 10.1 in both of the Awards, the Applicant submits that clause 37 of the Agreement by 
implication provides reasonably predictable hours of work. A second concern was raised about 
whether the Agreement being silent as to the safeguard provided for at clause 10.2 of the Clerks 
Award and 10.5 of the GRIA may result in any disadvantage to employees. These provisions 
in the Awards provide that hours of work are to be agreed in advance, in writing, at the 
commencement of an employee’s engagement, and specifying the number of hours worked 
each day, the days of the week the employee will work, and the shift times. The Applicant 
submits when clauses 35 and 37 of the Agreement are read together with current onboarding 
and rostering practices it is the case that sufficient safeguards are in place to ensure that part 
time employees do agree to their hours of work upfront.

---

**[8]** A further concern was raised in respect to whether the Agreement being silent as to the 
part time employees’ safeguard provided for at clause 10.3 - 10.4 of the Clerks Award 
pertaining to variations to hours and notice to changes to days worked may result in any 
disadvantage to employees. The Applicant submits that the provisions at clauses 35 and 38 of 
the Agreement operate to provide that variations to hours to be worked will be agreed in writing. 
The Applicant also indicates that clause 38 sets out that company initiated changes can only be 
made with 7 days’ notice, consistent with clause 10.4 of the Clerks Award. The final matter 
raised was in respect to part time safeguards in the Agreement being silent on all time worked 
in excess of ordinary hours agreed (or varied) being paid at the overtime rate applicable, as 
provided for at clause 10.6 of the Clerks Award and 10.8 of GRIA. In response the Applicant 
addressed this concern by clarifying that clause 19 relating to overtime for Retail Team 
Members and clause 28 relating to overtime for CCC Team Members provide that hours worked 
in excess of ordinary hours will be paid as overtime. Additionally, clause 17 b. relating to Retail 
Team Members and clause 26 b. relating to CCC Team Members provide that ordinary hours 
for team members employed on a part time basis will be the team member’s Core Hour (as 
determined or adjusted in accordance with clause 35) and will be less than 152 hours in each 4 
week roster period for team members employed on a part time basis.

**[9]** The Applicant also submits that the Agreement does not differ from a prior enterprise 
agreement in respect of part time safeguards and is of the view that its part time employees are 
a valued cohort of employees and many are supportive of approval. The Act was amended after 
the approval of the earlier enterprise agreement and the way the BOOT is applied has changed. 
The Commission may now consider reasonably foreseeable patterns or kinds of work or types 
of employment under the agreement by reference to the nature of the enterprise when applying 
the test. The Commission may also now, on application made under s. 227A, reconsider whether 
an agreement passes the BOOT where the patterns or kinds of work or types of employment 
differ either at the test time or a later time. In that regard I accept the explanations given about 
to the way the Agreement is intended to operate in relation to part time employees.

**[10]** Given the undertakings and having regard to s.193A(6), and in particular the patterns of 
work of the employees covered by the Agreement, I am satisfied that the BOOT is met. I note 
that should the work patterns, kinds of work or types of employment under the agreement
change, an application under s.227A is available for a reconsideration of the BOOT.

**[11]** A copy of the undertakings in relation to the matters raised under s. 186(2) (c) and (d) 
is attached in Annexure A. The terms of the undertakings were provided to all bargaining 
representatives. No objection was raised. I am satisfied that the undertakings will not cause 
financial detriment to any employee covered by the Agreement and will not result in substantial 
changes to the Agreement. Pursuant to s.201(3), the undertaking are taken to be terms of the 
Agreement.

**[12]** The Agreement does not cover all of the employees of the employer, however, taking 
into account the factors in sections 186(3) and (3A) I am satisfied that the group of employees 
was fairly chosen.

**[13]** Having regard to the material contained in the application and filed in relation to it, I am 
satisfied that each of the requirements of ss.186 and 187 are met.

**[14]** The Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees’ Association, being bargaining 
representatives for the Agreement, has given notice under s.183 of the Act that they want the

---

Agreement to cover it. In accordance with s.201(2) I note that the Agreement covers the 
organisations.

**[15]** The Agreement was approved on 2 May 2024 and, in accordance with s.54, will operate 
from 9 May 2024 rather than on Sunday 14 July 2024, or the first Sunday that is at least seven 
days after approval as specified at clause 6 of the Agreement. The nominal expiry date of the 
Agreement at clause 6 is 30 June 2027.

THE SEAL OF THE FAIR WORK COMMISSION

#### Section 1: COVERAGE

##### What is the title of the agreement?

1. This agreement shall be known as the Super Retail Group Retail & CCC Enterprise Agreement 2024, and 
replaces the Super Retail Group Enterprise Agreement 2018.

2. A copy of this agreement will be made accessible to team members in their workplace in hard and/or soft copy.

##### Who does this agreement apply to?

3. The parties to this agreement are:

a. Macpac Retail Pty Ltd  (**MAC);** and

b. Super Cheap Auto Pty Ltd (**SCA);** and

c. SRG Leisure Retail Pty Ltd (**SLR);** and

d. Super Retail Group Services Pty Ltd (**SRGS);** and

e. Rebel Sport Limited (**RSL);** and

f. any associated entity/ies (as that term is defined in the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth)) of the entities 
described in a. to e. which are established by **Super Retail Group** to assume the employer 
responsibilities of the above listed entities;

(a. to f. are collectively referred to as “**Super Retail Group”,** or “SRG”); and

g. subject to the exceptions listed in this agreement, waged team members engaged by SRG to perform 
work predominantly within the classifications contained within this agreement; and

h. the Shop Distributive and Allied Employees Association (**SDA).**

4. For the avoidance of doubt, this agreement does not cover or apply to:

a. any team member not covered by the classifications within this agreement (waged or salaried) 
including, but not limited to, Store Management and Support Office roles;

b. team members employed on a fixed or maximum term contract of employment and not performing 
work within the Retail and Customer Care Centre (“ **CCC**”) classifications contained within this 
agreement; and

c. any salaried team member who performs Set-up Work in a leadership role within a Set-up Team 
including, but not limited to: Assistant Store Improvement Manager; Store Improvement Manager; 
and Senior Store Improvement Manager.

5. This agreement will be read and interpreted in conjunction with the National Employment Standards (**NES).** 
Where there is an inconsistency between the agreement and the NES, and the NES provides a greater benefit, 
the NES provision will apply to the extent of the inconsistency.  Otherwise, subject to the Fair Work Act 2009 
(Cth) (**Act),** and except where this agreement expressly provides otherwise, this agreement operates to the 
exclusion of any other enterprise agreement, award, or industrial instrument.

##### When will this agreement commence and when will it expire?

6. This agreement will become operative on the later of Sunday 14 July 2024, or the first Sunday that is at least 
seven days after approval from the Fair Work Commission (**FWC).**  The Agreement nominally expires on 30 
June 2027 (**Nominal Expiry Date).**

7. The parties agree that up until the Nominal Expiry Date of this agreement:

a. they will not pursue any extra wage claims;

b. they will not seek any changes to conditions of employment;

c. this agreement will cover all matters or claims, which could otherwise be the subject of protected 
action; and

d. they will not engage in any industrial action, in relation to the performance of any work covered by 
this agreement, other than as permitted by the Act.

#### Section 2: PAYMENT OF WAGES

##### What Superannuation entitlements apply to team members?

8. Team members will be entitled to superannuation in accordance with Federal superannuation guarantee 
legislation. SRG will make required superannuation contributions to each team member’s nominated 
complying superannuation fund. If a team member does not nominate a superannuation fund, SRG will pay 
contributions to their stapled superannuation fund (if available), as advised by the Australian Tax Office (ATO). 
If SRG is unable to obtain details of a team member’s stapled superannuation fund from the ATO, or they do 
not have a stapled superannuation fund, then the required superannuation contributions will be made on the 
team member’s behalf into SRG's default superannuation fund, Retail Employees Superannuation Trust (REST). 
Superannuation guarantee contributions will be payable in respect of all ordinary time earnings, which includes 
hours paid at base rates or penalty rates (but excludes hours paid as overtime).

##### How will wages be paid?

9. Wages for the week Sunday to Saturday will be paid on the same day of each week by Electronic Funds 
Transfer (**EFT).**

10. Payment of wages may be altered from a weekly to a fortnightly basis if SRG provides team members with a 
minimum of 3 months’ notice of the change. If employed by SRG at the time when the pay frequency moves 
to a fortnightly pay, team members will be paid one week in advance with the additional pay able to be phased 
out progressively over a maximum period of 5 months, at the rate of one day after each completed month.

11. SRG will pay wages within 3 weekdays of the end of each pay period.  The pay day will be a fixed day.  In a rare 
event outside SRG’s control or a payroll system update, the payment day will not exceed 7 days from the end 
of the pay period.  SRG will give as much advanced notice as possible and offer hardship/team member loans 
to support cashflow.

12. SRG has the authority to deduct any pre-payments made from any money which is owed to a team member, if 
employment ends before they have earned the pre-paid amounts.

13. Should there be any pay discrepancy in a particular week or fortnight, then SRG will rectify that discrepancy 
within a reasonable time period.

##### What will team members be paid?

14. Team members will be paid equal to or greater than the rates of pay and other entitlements specified at 
**Appendix A.** No team member's Base Rate of pay will go backwards as a result of the operation of this 
Agreement.

15. For casual team members, the rate of pay specified in Appendix A is inclusive of a 25% casual loading, which is 
paid in lieu of payments for annual leave, redundancy pay and other entitlements associated with permanent 
employment.

16. To the extent permissible at law, where SRG inadvertently does not pay a Team Member correctly at the 
relevant time, SRG may offset the wages and entitlements paid to a Team Member under this agreement, and 
any above-agreement payments received by them excluding bonus and commission payments, against any 
entitlements (including but not limited to any ordinary hours, overtime, penalties, allowances, leave loadings 
and other loadings), that would otherwise have been payable to a team member under this agreement or 
applicable legislation (including the Fair Work Act):

a. across different pay periods or roster periods; and

b. even where those entitlements and the payments made as part of the remuneration are of an entirely 
different character or designation,

thereby reducing or satisfying in total any amount found to be owing to the Team Member.

---

Offsetting will only be against prior payments to the team member, unless agreed to by a team member in 
writing (in accordance with the Australian Taxation Office's overpayment recoupment rules), and the team 
member will be informed of any correction to the pay records to reflect the same.

# Section 3: HOURS OF WORK FOR RETAIL TEAM MEMBERS

##### Ordinary Hours for Retail Team Members

17. Subject to clauses 19 and 20 (overtime hours), ordinary hours of work will be:

a. 152 hours in each **4 week roster period** for team members employed on a full time basis;

b. the team member's Core Hours (as determined or adjusted in accordance with clause 35), and will be 
less than 152 hours in each **4 week roster period** for team members employed on a part time basis; 
or

c. less than 152 hours in each **4 week roster period** for team members employed on a casual basis.

##### Rostering Principles for Retail Team Members

18. Subject to clauses 19 and 20 (overtime hours), ordinary hours of work:

a. may not be worked on more than 10 days in each **2 week roster period;**

b. may not be worked on more than 6 consecutive days;

*c. will be rostered for team members in support of flexibility.  Team members may however elect in 
writing to receive one or more of the following:*

*i. receive a minimum of at least 2 consecutive days off in each* **_Adjusted 2 week roster period;_**

*ii. receive at least once in an* **_Adjusted 4 week roster period,_** *a weekend off (consecutive 
Saturday and Sunday);*

*iii. receive in the alternative to both (i) and (ii) above, two consecutive days off each week of the* 
**_Adjusted 2 week roster period,_** *or three consecutive days off in the* **_Adjusted 2 week roster 
period;_** *or*

*iv. for a team member who* **_regularly works Sundays,_** *receive three consecutive days off each* 
**_Adjusted 4 week roster period,_** *and the consecutive days off will include a Saturday and a 
Sunday.*

# Section 5: PART TIME CORE HOURS, ROSTER CHANGES AND BREAKS

##### Part Time Core Hours

b. in accordance with this clause and clauses 38, 39 and 40, the days on which Core Hours are worked

c. in a 4 week roster period team members may, by mutual agreement prior to working the hours, agree

of pay and treated as ordinary hours instead of overtime. SRG will record the team member’s 
agreement to work additional hours by variation to the team member’s roster.  The additional hours 
must comply with the rostering principles (see relevant clause 18 or 27) otherwise overtime may apply
(in accordance with relevant clause 20 or 29);

d. team members may request to reduce their Core Hours. Such request will be granted by SRG provided 
it does not interfere with operational requirements; and

e. changes to core hours may also occur at any time by mutual agreement.

*Example: a part time team member with agreed core hours of 80 hours in a 4 week roster period, can agree to 
work an additional 20 hours in the 4 week roster period to be paid at the ordinary or applicable penalty rate of 
pay in lieu of overtime by having those hours recorded in the roster. If the additional 20 hours is agreed and 
rostered in this way, then overtime under clause 19 will only apply to hours in excess of 100 hours (ie: 80 + 20 
hours) worked in the 4 week roster period.*

a regular and systematic basis, in excess of their Core Hours, the team member may request in writing to 
increase their Core Hours to the level of those regular and systematic hours.  SRG will not unreasonably refuse 
such a request.

*Example: A part time team member whose Core Hours are 12 per week has over the past 12 months been 
working a regular and systematic roster which involves them working 22 hours per week (in some weeks the 
team member also works some additional hours over the 22 hours to meet operational needs). The team 
member can, at the end of the 12 month period, request that their core hours be increased to 22 per week, and* 
*SRG will not unreasonably refuse the request. Examples of where a refusal will generally be reasonable are if 
the team member is working the additional hours due to long term absence of another team member or where 
the workplace is experiencing challenges in attracting and retaining team members.*

as leave loading, over those two weeks, provided you have accrued sufficient leave to cover this.*

65. In addition, team members will also be paid annual leave loading, being the greater of:

a. 17.5% annual leave loading; or

b. The relevant weekend or late night pay rate loading (i.e. the % above Permanent Base Rate).

---

66. When annual leave is requested and approved, a request may be made (without prior approval being 
required from SRG) to receive payment for that leave, in full upon commencement of the leave, or during the 
leave.

67. Annual leave does not include any public holidays which fall during the annual leave period, provided those 
public holidays fall on days that would have ordinarily been worked had the leave not been taken.

68. Where a team member has an accrued balance of annual leave on termination of their employment, or 
where their employment status changes from permanent to casual employment, the accrued annual leave 
will be paid out at the Permanent Base Rate, plus 17.5% annual leave loading, in the next pay cycle following 
the date of termination or effective date of the change in employment status.

###### Cashing out leave

69. Taking annual leave is important to the wellbeing of team members, and SRG encourages team to take 
annual leave. However, team members are entitled to forgo an entitlement to paid annual leave, and instead 
be paid for that accrued leave, subject to the following conditions:

a. The team member must not cash out an amount of paid annual leave that would result in a remaining 
accrued annual leave balance of less than 4 weeks;

b. each annual leave cash out request must be made by a separate agreement in writing; and

c. annual leave cashed out must be paid in the same amount that would have been paid had the leave 
been taken at the time of making the cash out request.

##### Personal / Carer’s Leave

###### Accrual of leave

70. Full time team members accrue 10 days of paid personal / carer’s leave for each year of paid service. Part 
time team members accrue paid personal / carer’s leave on a pro rata basis based on the ordinary hours of 
work. Casual team members are not entitled to paid personal/carer’s leave.

71. Personal / carer’s leave entitlements accrue progressively from year to year and will accrue on the basis of 
1/26<sup>th</sup> of the number of ordinary hours worked each pay period.

*Example: If you are a part time team member and work 26 ordinary hours in one week, you will accrue 1 hour 
of personal / carer’s leave for that week.*

72. Personal / carer’s leave will accrue during periods of paid leave, including SRG Paid Parental Leave, but will 
not accrue during a period of unpaid leave.

###### Taking leave

73. Team members are entitled to take personal / carer’s leave if:

a. they are suffering from a personal illness or injury that means they are unable to attend work (sick 
leave); or

b. they are providing care and support for a member of their immediate family or household who 
requires that care and support because of:

i. a personal illness or injury affecting the member; or

ii. an unexpected emergency affecting the member (carer’s leave).

74. Team members may utilise paid personal / carer’s leave in circumstances where they are experiencing 
domestic and family violence in accordance with SRG’s Support for Victims of Domestic and Family Violence 
Policy as applicable from time to time. The Policy does not form part of this agreement.

###### Payment for leave

75. When taking paid personal / carer’s leave, team members will be paid for such leave at their Permanent Base 
Rate for the ordinary hours that would have been worked on that day or days. There is no entitlement to be paid out any accrued paid personal /carer’s leave on termination of employment, or a change in employment 
status from permanent to casual employment.

###### Unpaid carer’s leave

76. Team members, including casuals, are entitled to 2 days unpaid carer’s leave for each occasion when a 
member of the team member’s immediate family, or member of the team member’s household requires care 
and support for the circumstances outlined in clauses 73 and 74.

###### Notice and evidence

77. In order to take paid personal / carer’s leave a team member must:

a. verbally notify their direct manager as soon as reasonably practicable that the shift will not be 
attended and advise them of the period of leave expected to be taken; and

b. if requested, supply evidence that would satisfy a reasonable person (for example, a medical 
certificate from a registered medical practitioner) as evidence of the entitlement to the leave.

78. If unable to provide a medical certificate, or the absence is for carer’s leave, SRG may require a statutory 
declaration setting out the reason why the team member was unable to attend work.

79. Team members will generally be required to supply satisfactory evidence to substantiate their absence if:

a. more than 5 days sick leave is taken, without a medical certificate or other satisfactory evidence, in 
any 12 month period;

b. the absence is for 2 or more consecutive working days;

c. the absence is due to illness or injury and the team member has exhausted all personal / carer’s leave 
entitlements (and are not receiving workers’ compensation payments);

d. the team member is absent on a day before or after a public holiday or day on which they are not 
required to work; or

e. there are concerns about the genuineness of the claim to personal / carer’s leave, for example where 
SRG has identified that there is a pattern to personal leave taken. Without limiting what may lead to 
a concern, it may include where the same day of the week is taken off sick on 3 or more occasions 
without providing satisfactory evidence.

Where a team member takes personal/carers leave for the purpose of taking primary care responsibilities of a 
person who is frail or aged or has a long-term disability or illness, evidence can be provided every 12 weeks 
instead of on each occasion (or as otherwise agreed with the team member and their manager).

80. For the purposes of personal / carer’s leave and compassionate leave:

a. ‘ **child**’ includes an adopted child, stepchild, foster child, child under a Permanent Care Order, an exnuptial child, or an adult child;
*Note: the inclusion of a stillborn child or miscarriage in compassionate leave at clause 81.*

b. ‘ **close immediate family**’ means a team member’s spouse, sibling, child, or parent, or the child of their 
spouse;

c. ‘ **foster child**’ means a child who is formally placed with the team member on a permanent/long term 
care arrangement and includes immediate/crisis, short term or respite care arrangements;

d. ‘ **household**’ includes relatives or other persons who ordinarily live in the same domestic dwelling as 
the team member;

e. ’ **immediate family**’ means:

i. the spouse, child, foster child, parent/step-parent, grandparent/step-grandparent, 
grandchild/step-grandchild, sibling/step-sibling or guardian of the team member; or

ii. a child, parent/step-parent, grandparent/step-grandparent, grandchild/step-grandchild, 
sibling/step-sibling or guardian of the team member’s spouse;

---

f. **‘child under a Permanent Care Order’** means a child for which a team member is a Permanent 
Guardian subject to a Permanent Care Order;

g. ‘ **spouse**’ includes a team member’s current or former spouse, civil union partner, or de facto partner 
irrespective of whether the persons are of the same gender or different genders.

##### Compassionate Leave

81. Full time and part time team members are entitled to 2 days paid compassionate leave on each occasion if:

a. a member of their immediate family or household as defined in this agreement, or their foster child:

i. contracts or develops a personal illness or sustains a personal injury that poses a serious 
threat to his or her life; or

ii. passes away; or

b. a child is stillborn and that child would have been a member of their immediate family or household 
as defined in this agreement, if the child had been born alive; or

c. the team member or the team member’s spouse has a miscarriage, or a former spouse of a team 
member has a miscarriage.

82. Full time and part time team members are entitled to up to an additional 3 days paid compassionate leave 
where a member of their close immediate family passes away.

83. Casual team members are entitled to compassionate leave in accordance with clause 81 and 82 on an unpaid 
basis.

84. Full or part time team members will be paid compassionate leave at their Permanent Base Rate for the 
ordinary hours they would have worked on the day or days.

85. Where interstate travel is required for the purpose of compassionate leave, team members are entitled to 
access 2 days annual leave, or 2 days unpaid leave for casual team members.

86. To substantiate an absence, team members may be required to supply evidence that would satisfy a 
reasonable person.

#### Section 7: OTHER LEAVE (including Community Service Leave)

##### Community Service Leave

87. Team members’ entitlement to Community Service Leave will be as per the NES unless this agreement 
provides for more beneficial entitlements.

##### Emergency Services Leave

88. Subject to SRG’s approval, full time, part time and casual team members are entitled to 3 days paid 
Emergency Services leave, per calendar year.

89. Emergency Services Leave applies if the team member is required to carry out duties with the State 
Emergency Service, Country Fire Authority, or other recognised emergency service organisation in an
emergency situation.

90. Emergency Services Leave is not cumulative and will not be paid out on termination of employment. SRG
may request evidence of appointment to, or service with, a registered emergency service provider.

##### Jury Service

91. There may be occasions when team members are summoned to perform jury duty. Full time, part time and 
casual (to the extent permitted by relevant State and Territory legislation) team members will be allowed a 
leave of absence during any period when they are required to attend for jury service. If employed on a casual 
basis in a State or Territory that does not allow a paid leave of absence, team members are encouraged to 
update their availability within Dimensions for periods of jury service.

92. If the team member is allowed a leave of absence for jury service, then during that leave of absence and 
subject to applicable legislation (including applicable State and Territory legislation), they will be paid the 
difference between:

a. the jury service fees that they are receiving; and

b. their Ordinary Time Earnings for the period that they are attending jury service.
*Note: Practically, SRG pays the team member their ordinary times earnings for the period, and then 
seeks reimbursement from the team member for jury service fees received.*

93. The team member will be required to provide SRG with proof of the jury service fees that they received and 
also proof of their requirement to attend and their attendance at jury service.

94. The team member must give SRG notice of the requirement for them to attend jury service as soon as 
practicable after receiving notification to attend.

95. When on jury service, the team member will not be required to attend work until the completion of that jury 
service. However, in States and Territories where it is permitted, if jury service on any day is less than four 
hours and the team member’s ordinary rostered hours of work would otherwise be worked later or earlier in 
the day, then they may be required to report to work for their total number of hours rostered that day less 
the time spent on jury service, unless there are less than 3 hours left (minimum shift), or unless otherwise 
agreed.

*Example: If rostered shift was 10am – 5.30pm (7 hours worked), and the team member attended jury duty 9-*
*11am, arrive at work at 12pm, the team member should then work until 4.30pm (reflecting the fact that they 
started Jury Service at 9am.   In Dimensions, they will record the 4.5 hours between 12 and 430pm as worked 
time, and the remaining 2.5 hours as jury duty leave.*

96. When on jury service, the team member will also be allowed a leave of absence without loss of pay for jury 
service for any day they would normally work so that the combination of jury service and ordinary work days 
does not exceed the number of days on which they would normally be required to work ordinary hours in 
that week.

---

*Example: a team member who normally works a 5 day week Tuesday to Saturday who is required to attend 
jury service for 5 days on Monday to Friday, will not be required to work the Saturday so that they are not 
required to work or attend jury duty for more than 5 days (the number of days they would normally work) in 
the week.*

##### Blood Donor Leave

97. If employed on a full time or part time basis, a team member may with SRG’s prior approval be absent during 
their ordinary working hours (i.e. during one of their normal rostered shifts) for the purpose of donating 
blood. The team member will be paid up to a maximum of 2 hours on each occasion and subject to a 
maximum of 4 separate absences for the purpose of donating blood each calendar year.

98. The team member intending to donate blood must agree the time and date of their absence in advance with 
their Supervisor or Manager to be on a day suitable to SRG and to be as close as possible to the beginning or 
ending of their ordinary working hours. Team Members should consider Red Cross guidance regarding 
physical activity before and after donation.

99. To be entitled to blood donor leave, the team member will need to provide proof of attendance at a 
recognised place for the purpose of donating blood and the duration of such attendance.

##### Study Leave

100.Team members may apply for unpaid study leave up to 2 weeks per calendar year for the purpose of 
preparing for and participating in exams and assignments.

101.Study leave may be taken in a continuous period or in single day absences.

102.Study leave does not include any training that team members are directed by SRG to undertake.

103.Team members must make a written application for study leave at least 1 month in advance.

104.SRG will endeavour wherever possible to accommodate requests for study leave. However, in the granting of 
study leave, factors including team member attendance record and the stores’ operational requirements, will 
be taken into account.

105.Any period of unpaid study leave will not count as service for the calculation of other leave entitlements 
under this agreement.

##### Natural Disaster Leave

106.Subject to SRG’s approval, permanent and casual team members will be entitled to up to 3 days paid leave in 
any calendar year for the purpose of natural disaster leave.

107.To be eligible for natural disaster leave team members must be unable to attend work because of a natural 
disaster. A natural disaster may include a flood, cyclone, storm surge or fire.

108.Team members will be paid natural disaster leave at their Base Rate of pay for the ordinary hours they would 
have worked on the day or days.

109.At SRG’s discretion, SRG may approve additional days of natural disaster leave until team members are able 
to return to work. Any additional days of natural disaster leave will be unpaid leave unless team members
choose to access any of their accrued annual leave or long service leave entitlements.

110.Natural disaster leave is not cumulative and will not be paid out on termination of employment.

---

##### Defence Force Reserves Leave

111.SRG may approve team members to take up to 2 weeks leave in any calendar year for the purpose of Defence 
Force Reserves leave.

112.To be eligible for Defence Force Reserves leave team members must be a member of the Australian Defence 
Force Reserves and such leave must be for the purpose of participating in training camps, or equivalent 
continuous duty.

113.Defence Force Reserves leave will be unpaid leave unless team members choose to access any of their 
accrued annual leave or long service leave entitlements.

114.At SRG’s discretion, SRG may approve additional days of Defence Force Reserves leave. Any additional days of 
Defence Force Reserves leave will be unpaid leave unless team members choose to access any of their 
accrued annual leave or long service leave entitlements.

115.If team members request Defence Force Reserves leave, they must furnish evidence of their entitlement to 
such leave before SRG will approve it.

##### Family and Domestic Violence Leave

116.SRG is committed to providing support to team members that experience family or domestic violence and 
will treat all such matters with confidentiality. Please see SRG’s Support for Victims of Family and Domestic 
Violence Policy (which can be found on our <u>Policy Portal</u>) for further information.

117.All team members, including permanent and casual team members, are entitled to access ten (10) days paid

b. attending court appearances;

c. attending counselling.

119.Other support that SRG can make available to team members in a family or domestic violence situation may

b. temporary flexible work arrangements and formal flexible work arrangements; or

personal / carer’s leave because they or a member of their immediate family is experiencing domestic 
violence such as a medical certificate, a document issued by the police service or a court, or a statutory

---

In addition, all team members are entitled to 5 days’ unpaid leave to deal with family and domestic violence, 
as follows:

a. such leave is available in full at the start of each 12-month period of the team member’s 
employment; and

b. does not accumulate from year to year.

#### Section 8: PUBLIC HOLIDAYS

##### Public Holidays

###### What is the definition of Public Holiday?

123.For the purpose of this agreement, the following days shall be public holidays:

a. 1 January (New Year’s Day);

b. 26 January (Australia Day);

c. Good Friday;

d. Easter Monday;

e. 25 April (Anzac Day);

f. 25 December (Christmas Day);

g. the King’s / Queen’s birthday holiday (on the day on which it is celebrated in a State or Territory or a 
region of a State or Territory);

h. 26 December (Boxing Day); and

i. any other day declared to be a public holiday by or under a law of the State or Territory in which the 
team member is principally engaged to perform work, other than a day, or kind of day, that is excluded 
by the regulations made for the purposes of the Act from counting as a public holiday, and

j. if, in any calendar year, only 10 public holidays have been declared as public holidays in any State or 
Territory, then one additional day shall be considered a Public Holiday for the purpose of this 
agreement as follows:

i. in Western Australia– Easter Saturday;

ii. in New South Wales – the first Tuesday in November;

iii. in all other states and territories – a day nominated by SRG.

124.If, under a law of a State or Territory, a day or part-day is substituted for a day or part-day that would 
otherwise be a public holiday because of clause 123, then the substituted day or part-day is the public 
holiday. Where such substitution occurs, the entitlements set out in this agreement will apply on the 
substituted day only, and the actual day set out in clause 123 above will be treated as an ordinary working 
day and will not attract public holiday rates.

###### What are team members’ public holiday entitlements?

125.All team members employed on a full time or part time basis are entitled to a day off on a public holiday 
without loss of pay. However, team members may be requested to work on a public holiday.

126.If team members work on a public holiday:

a. team members will be paid for any ordinary hours that they work on the day at the public holiday rate 
for their classification; and

b. if employed on a full time or part time basis and unless agree otherwise, team members will be 
rostered to work at least the same number of ordinary hours that they would ordinarily be required 
to work on that day of the week if it were not a public holiday. If SRG provide team members with a 
lesser number of ordinary hours on the public holiday, then the difference in hours will be paid to 
team members at their Permanent Base Rate; and

c. if employed on a permanent or casual basis and team members are required to work overtime on a 
public holiday then those overtime hours will be paid at the relevant Public Holiday Overtime Rate in 
Appendix A.

*Example: If you are a full time team member, and usually work 7.6 hours per day, but only work 6 hours on 
a public holiday, you will be entitled to be paid for 6 hours at the public holiday rate for your classification 
and 1.6 hours at your Base Rate.*

127.If team members do not work on a public holiday:

a. if employed on a full time or part time basis, and the team member would ordinarily be required to 
work on that day of the week if it were not a public holiday, then:

---

i. If the team member decides not to work the public holiday, or is otherwise not required to 
work, then the team member will be paid their normal rostered ordinary hours for that day 
at their Permanent Base Rate (“Public Holiday Rostered Not Worked” entitlement);

ii. If the public holiday falls during a period that the team member was on paid leave, then no 
leave will be deducted for this day, and the “Public Holiday Rostered Not Worked” 
entitlement will apply;

iii. If the public holiday falls during a period that the team member was on unpaid leave 
directly before and after a Public Holiday, then the public holiday is unpaid.

b. if the team member would not ordinarily be required to work on that day of the week if it were not 
a public holiday, then there is no public holiday entitlement for the team member if they do not 
work.

c. if the team member is employed on a casual basis, then there is no public holiday entitlement for 
the team member if they do not work.

###### Work on public holidays

128.Team members acknowledge that given the nature of SRG’s business it is necessary for SRG to trade on public 
holidays and therefore to meet the operational demands SRG requires work to be performed on those days.

129.At least 21 days in advance, SRG will call for volunteers to work during the following times:

a. on a public holiday; and

b. on any day that is declared under a law of a State or Territory to be a ‘substituted day’; and

c. after 6pm on either:

i. 24 December; or

ii. 31 December.

130.If after calling for volunteers as per clause 129, there are insufficient volunteers to meet the operational 
needs, then subject to clause 131 SRG may request team members to work during these times. When 
deciding whether or not to request team members to work at these times SRG will consider the number of 
holidays that team members have been given off in the past in comparison with other team members in their 
workplace. A request to work may be made either:

a. through a direct request to a team member prior to draft rosters being released; or

b. in the form of a draft roster, noting that team members can indicate if they accept or refuse a 
proposed public holiday shift before the final roster is confirmed.

131.If team members are requested to work on a public holiday listed in clause 123, then they may refuse to do 
so only if they have reasonable grounds for refusing such a request. When considering whether or not team 
members have reasonable grounds for refusing such a request, SRG will have regard to those factors as set 
out in section 114 (4) of the Act.

132.The 21 days’ notice specified in clause 129 will be shortened if the declaration of the public holiday occurs 
less than 21 days before the date of the public holiday. In such circumstances, SRG will provide notice as 
soon as practicable after becoming aware of the newly declared public holiday.

133.If the Christmas Day public holiday is substituted to a day other than 25 December, and 25 December is then 
not separately declared a public holiday in that State, any work performed on 25 December will be paid at the 
relevant Public Holiday Penalty rate in Appendix A.

#### Section 9: TERMINATION, REDUNDANCY AND CONSULTATION

##### What notice period is required to terminate employment?

134.Permanent team members may have their employment terminated by either SRG or the team member giving 
at least the following notice in writing or, in the case of termination by SRG, payment in lieu of notice (based 
on the amount the team member would have received had they continued working during their notice 
period, including penalties, loadings, allowances and other separately identifiable entitlements):

| Period of continuous service | Period of notice |
| --- | --- |
| 1 year or less | 1 week |
| More than 1 year and up to 3 years | 2 weeks |
| More than 3 years and up to 5 years | 3 weeks |
| More than 5 years | 4 weeks |

135.If team members are 45 years of age or older with at least two years of continuous service then SRG must 
give them one extra week of notice if SRG terminates their employment.

136.If team members terminate their employment and do not give SRG the right amount of notice in clause 134,
SRG can withhold an amount from their final pay equal to the Ordinary Time Earnings that they would have 
earned for the period of notice that they failed to give. SRG may agree to reduce the amount of notice that 
the team member is required to give.

137.There is no requirement for SRG to give team members notice of termination:

a. if they are employed on a casual basis; or

b. if they are employed on a fixed term or fixed task basis; or

c. where their employment is terminated because of serious misconduct (which includes, but is not 
limited to: drunkenness, theft, fraud, assault, refusal to carry out a lawful and reasonable instruction, 
conduct that causes a serious and imminent risk to health and safety, or the reputation, viability, or 
profitability of SRG’s business); or

d. if they are a team member to whom a training arrangement applies and whose employment is for a 
specified period of time or is, for any reason, limited to the duration of the training arrangement and 
the employment is terminated at the end of that period.

##### Abandoning employment

138.If team members are absent from work for 3 or more consecutive shifts, without SRG’s consent and without 
notification to SRG, they may be deemed by SRG to have abandoned their employment. Subject to 
reasonable endeavours by SRG to contact the team member and there being no genuine reason for their 
failure to notify us, SRG will then be entitled to terminate the team members’ employment with notice.

139.If a team member fails to attend work during the relevant notice period without prior approval the team 
member will not be entitled to payment for any time not worked.

##### What if a team member’s position is made redundant?

140.Sometimes it is necessary to terminate the employment of a team member because their position has been 
made redundant.

141.Subject to the Act, if a team member is employed on a full time or part time basis and their position becomes 
redundant then SRG’s preferred option is to transfer the team member to an acceptable alternative position rather than terminating their employment. If this occurs, team members will not be entitled to any severance 
pay, but if they are employed on a full time or part time basis they will be entitled to be given notice of the 
change, in accordance with the notice periods in either clause 134 or 135. If the alternative position is a lower 
paid position then their Permanent Base Rate will be maintained at the higher rate for the notice period.

142.Subject to clauses 141 and 143, if a team member’s employment is terminated because their position is 
redundant, then they will be entitled to be paid severance pay in accordance with the following table:

| Years of Continuous Service | Severance Pay (If team member is under 45 years of age) | Severance Pay (If team member is 45 years of age or older) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Less than 1 year | Nil | Nil |
| 1 year but not more than 2 years | 4 weeks' pay | 5 weeks' pay |
| More than 2 years but not more than 3 years | 7 weeks' pay | 8.75 weeks' pay |
| More than 3 years but not more than 4 years | 10 weeks' pay | 12.5 weeks' pay |
| More than 4 years but not more than 5 years | 12 weeks' pay | 15 weeks' pay |
| More than 5 years but not more than 6 years | 14 weeks' pay | 17.5 weeks' pay |
| More than 6 years | 16 weeks' pay | 20 weeks' pay |

143.Severance payments will be calculated based on team member’s Ordinary Time Earnings.

144.Subject to clause 145, if SRG makes the decision to terminate a team member’s employment because their 
position is made redundant, then they will be allowed up to one day’s time off without loss of pay during 
each week of the notice period for the purpose of seeking other employment. If they have been allowed 
paid leave for more than one day during the notice period for the purpose of seeking other employment, 
they will, at SRG’s request, be required to produce proof of attendance at a job interview or they will not 
receive payment for the time absent. For this purpose a statutory declaration will be sufficient.

145.Team members will not be entitled to severance payments or the entitlement contained within clause 142, 
if:

a. they are employed on a casual basis;

b. they are employed on a fixed term or fixed task basis;

c. the FWC makes an order to that effect;

d. they are offered employment in an alternative position (including with any of the employers that are 
party to this agreement) and that offer contains terms and conditions that are substantially similar to 
and no less favourable, considered on an overall basis, than the terms and conditions applicable to 
them immediately prior to their original position being made redundant; or

e. the business or part of the business is transmitted from SRG (“current employer”) to another entity 
(“the new employer”), and:

i. they receive an offer of employment from the new employer; and

ii. that offer contains terms and conditions that are substantially similar and no less favourable, 
considered on an overall basis, than the terms and conditions applicable to the team member 
at the time of ceasing employment with SRG; and

iii. the offer provides that the new employer will recognise the period of continuous service 
that they had with SRG to be continuous service with the new employer.

##### What is SRG’s duty to consult about the introduction of major changes?

146.Where SRG has made a definite decision to introduce major changes in production, program, organisation, 
structure or technology that are likely to have significant effects on team members, SRG will notify and 
consult with those team members.

147.“Significant effects” include termination of employment, major changes in the composition, operation or size 
of SRG’s workforce or in the skills required; the elimination or diminution of job opportunities, promotion 
opportunities or job tenure, the alteration of hours of work, the need for retraining or transfer of team 
members to other work locations and the restructuring of jobs. An exception to these cases will be where this 
agreement makes provision for alterations of any of the matters referred to in this clause. In those cases the 
alteration will be deemed not to have significant effect.

148.SRG will discuss with the team members affected the introduction of the changes referred to in clause 146, 
the effects that the changes are likely to have on team members and measures to avert or mitigate the 
adverse effects of such changes on team members.

149.The discussions between SRG and affected team members will commence as early as practicable after a 
definite decision has been made by SRG to make the changes referred to in clause 146.

150.For the purposes of the discussions, SRG will provide in writing to the team members concerned all relevant 
information about the changes including the nature of the changes proposed, the expected effects of the 
changes on team members and any other matters likely to affect team members, provided that SRG will not 
be required to disclose any confidential information.

151.The parties may appoint a representative for the purposes of this consultation process. Team members may 
appoint an official of the union as their representative.

##### What is SRG’s duty to consult about roster changes?

152.SRG will consult team members employed on a full time or part time basis about a proposed change to their 
regular roster, standard shift patterns or ordinary hours of work.

153.When consulting team members about a change to their regular roster, standard shift patterns or ordinary 
hours of work, SRG must:

##### ‘Regular Casual’ conversion to permanent employment

179.For the purpose of clauses 180 to 197, a **'regular casual'** is a casual team member who has been employed by 
SRG for a period of 12 months and has during at least the last 6 months of employment, worked a regular 
pattern of hours on an ongoing basis which, without significant adjustment, the team member could continue 
to perform as a full-time or part-time team member under the provisions of this agreement.

###### Offers to convert

180.If team members are engaged by SRG as a **regular casual** then SRG will make an offer in writing of full-time or 
part-time employment (dependent on whether the team member was working the equivalent of full time or 
part time hours in the last 6 months before the offer) to that team member after 12 months of employment.  
The offer will be made within 21 days after the end of the 12 month period, unless there are **reasonable 
grounds** (as defined in clause 189) not to make an offer.

181.SRG will provide written notice to all regular casual team members who have been employed by SRG for a 
period of 12 months but are not being offered casual conversion, which will include details of the reasons for 
not making an offer, within 21 days after the end of the 12 month period.

182.Team members must give SRG a written response to the offer within 21 days after the offer is given, stating 
whether the team member accepts or declines the offer.  The team member will be taken to have declined the 
offer if they do not provide a written response as prescribed.

183.Within 21 days of a team member accepting an offer, SRG must comply with clause 192.

###### Requests to convert

184.A team member is not eligible to make a request as outlined within clauses 185 or 186 if in the last 6 months 
before the request:

a. They have refused an offer by SRG to convert to permanent employment;

---

b. SRG has informed them in writing that they are not receiving an offer to convert to permanent 
employment because there was a reasonable ground not to make the offer; or

c. SRG has refused a prior request for casual conversion because there was a reasonable ground to 
refuse the request.

185.If team members are a **regular casual** and have worked equivalent full-time hours over the preceding period 
of 6 months’ they may request to have their employment converted to full-time employment.

186.If team members are a **regular casual** and have worked less than equivalent full-time hours over the preceding 
period of 6 months’ they may request to have their employment converted to part-time employment 
consistent with the pattern of hours previously worked.

187.Any request for casual conversion must be in writing and provided to management.

188.Upon receiving any such request, SRG must give the team member a written response within 21 days after 
request is made to SRG stating whether SRG agrees to the request and will offer conversion, or refuses the 
request (including reasons if the request is refused).  The request may only be refused on **reasonable grounds**
(as defined in clause 189) and after there has been consultation with the team member.  Where SRG agrees to 
the request and will offer conversion, SRG must also comply with clause 192 within the same 21 day period.

###### Reasonable grounds not to convert

189.Reasonable grounds for refusal or not making an offer to convert a casual employee include that:

a. it would require a significant adjustment to the team member’s hours of work in order for them to 
be engaged on a full-time or part-time basis in accordance with the provisions of this agreement;

b. it is known or reasonably foreseeable that their position will cease to exist within the next 12 
months;

c. it is known or reasonably foreseeable that the hours of work which they are required to perform will 
be significantly reduced in the next 12 months; or

d. it is known or reasonably foreseeable that there will be a significant change in the days and/or times 
at which their hours of work are required to be performed in the next 12 months which cannot be 
accommodated within the days and/or hours during which they are available to work.

190.For any ground of refusal to be reasonable, it must be based on facts which are known or reasonably 
foreseeable.

191.If the team member does not accept SRG’s refusal, this will constitute a dispute that will be dealt with under 
the dispute resolution procedure in <u>Section 11:</u> Dispute Resolution Procedure and the matter may be referred 
to the FWC if the dispute cannot be resolved at the workplace level.

###### General provisions

192.Where it is agreed that team members will have their employment converted to full-time or part-time 
employment as provided for in this clause, SRG will discuss with them and record in writing:

a. the form of employment to which they will convert – that is, full-time or part-time employment;

b. the hours of work after conversion takes effect;

c. the day the team member's conversion to full-time or part-time employment takes effect; and

d. if it is agreed that they will become a part-time team member, the matters referred to in clause 35.

193.The conversion will take effect from the start of the next pay cycle following such agreement being reached 
unless otherwise agreed.

194.If team members convert to permanent employment, they may request to revert back to casual employment 
with SRG’s express written agreement.

195.SRG must not engage and re-engage team members (which includes a refusal to re-engage), or reduce or vary 
their hours of work in order to avoid any right or obligation under this casual conversion process.

196.Nothing in this casual conversion process obliges team members to convert to full-time or part-time 
employment.

---

197.Nothing in this clause requires SRG to increase team members hours of work if they are seeking conversion to 
full-time or part-time employment.

#### Section 11: DISPUTE RESOLUTION PROCEDURE

##### What types of disputes does this procedure apply to?

207.The dispute resolution procedure in this section applies to disputes about matters arising under this 
agreement or the National Employment Standards between SRG and team member(s).

208.In this section, ‘parties’ means a party to the dispute or the parties to the dispute.

209.The parties may separately appoint a representative of their choosing for the purposes of the procedures in 
this section.

##### The parties must firstly attempt to resolve the dispute at the workplace level

210.Firstly, there must be a genuine attempt to resolve any disputes at the workplace level between the team 
member(s) involved and their immediate supervisor(s).

211.If the dispute remains unresolved or it is inappropriate for the matter to be dealt with between the team 
member(s) involved and their immediate Supervisor(s), there must be a genuine attempt to resolve the 
dispute via discussions between the team member(s) involved and their next level of management.

212.If the dispute remains unresolved, there must be a genuine attempt to resolve the dispute via discussions 
between the team member(s) involved and SRG’s Human Resource representative.

##### What is the process if the dispute cannot be resolved at the workplace level?

213.If the dispute is unable to be resolved at the workplace level, and all of the steps referred to in clauses 210 to 
212 have been taken, either party to the dispute may refer the matter(s) in dispute to the FWC.

214.The FWC may deal with the dispute in 2 stages:

a. The FWC will first attempt to resolve the dispute as it considers appropriate, including by mediation, 
conciliation, expressing an opinion or making a recommendation; and

b. if the FWC is unable to resolve the dispute at the first stage, the FWC may then:

i. arbitrate the dispute; and

ii. make a determination that is binding on the parties.

##### Whilst the dispute is being resolved

215.While the dispute is being resolved, work must continue as usual.

a. If the dispute relates to a change in conditions of employment, including but not limited to rosters, 
trading hours and/or times and flexibility arrangements, and the dispute is notified in writing by the 
team member within 3 days of being issued notice of the change, SRG will not enact the change 
within 25 calendar days of receiving the team member’s written submission.  The parties must 
continue genuine attempts to resolve the dispute during this period.  If the dispute relates to terms 
and conditions of employment already in place, work must continue as usual while the dispute is 
resolved.

# Section 12: FLEXIBILITY TERMS

##### Flexible Work Arrangements

216.SRG recognises that team members have many commitments between their personal lives and work, and that 
these responsibilities are specific to each individual and change over time.  That is why SRG offers team 
members a vast range of flexible work arrangements to ensure freedom and choice to work around their 
lifestyle, while still getting the most out of their time at work.

217.Flexible work arrangements are changes to the standard hours, pattern and/or location of work. There are 
many ways in which team members may work flexibly, in line with operational needs whilst meeting the needs 
of customers and stakeholders. To achieve the best outcomes for all of SRG, team members and people 
leaders need to work together to discuss their needs and expectations relating to flexible work arrangements, 
and explore the options available. Examples of flexible work arrangements can include: condensed working 
weeks like 4-day weeks, or 9-day fortnights; or modified standard working hours, or working days.

218.In addition to Individual Flexibility Arrangements (covered in clause 219) SRG offers flexible work 
arrangements as per the NES or better as outlined in SRG’s **Flexible Work Practices Guide.** In accordance with 
that guide, there is no minimum length of service requirement, and all SRG team members may request 
flexible working arrangements.

##### Individual Flexibility Arrangements

219.Notwithstanding any other provision of this agreement, SRG may agree with team members to vary the 
application of certain terms of this agreement to meet the genuine needs of SRG and team members on an 
individual basis. Those terms relate to the following:

a. arrangements for when work is performed;

b. overtime rates;

c. penalty rates;

d. allowances; and

e. leave loading.

220.SRG is required to ensure that any individual flexibility arrangement agreed under this clause:

a. is about matters that are permitted under the Act;

b. does not include a term that would be an unlawful under the Act;

c. is in writing, names the parties to the individual flexibility arrangement and is signed by SRG and the 
team member and, if they are under 18 years of age, their parent or guardian;

d. states each term of this agreement that the parties have agreed to vary;

e. details how the application of each term has been varied by agreement between the parties;

f. has been genuinely made without coercion or duress;

g. results in the team member being better off overall than they would have been if no individual 
flexibility arrangement had been agreed to;

h. details how the individual flexibility arrangement results in the team member being better off 
overall;

i. states the date upon which the individual flexibility arrangement commences to operate; and
j. specifies that the arrangement may be terminated:

i. by either party giving not more than 28 days’ notice of termination, in writing, to the other 
party; or

ii. at any time, by written agreement between the team member and SRG.

221.SRG will give team members a copy of the individual flexibility arrangement within 14 days after it is agreed 
to.

222.The individual flexibility arrangement must not require the approval or consent of a person other than SRG
and team member (unless they are under 18 years of age in which case approval of their parent or guardian is 
required).

223.The right to make an agreement pursuant to this clause is in addition to, and is not intended to otherwise 
affect, any provision for an agreement between team members and SRG contained in any other term of this 
enterprise agreement.

###### Admin Level 1 - Contact Consultant

254.A team member appointed as a Contact Consultants will be required to undertake a varying range of 
responsibilities. These responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

a. Follow all WHS procedures

b. Under general supervision, or within a prescribed training program for contact handing:

i. Able to respond to enquiries across one or more contact centre channels

ii. Can use one or more of the required technologies for contact handling

of work

products and services, but is generally dependent on responding to contacts using documented practices, 
procedures and instructions

###### Admin Level 2 – Experienced Consultant

Consultant, based on their completed training, demonstrated knowledge and adherence to process standards, 
with an ability to resolve all general enquiry types.

257.The responsibilities of an Experienced Consultant may include, but are not limited to:

a. Able to work with minimal or no supervision

b. Operate all technology systems utilised within the contact centre

c. Manage all contact types to required quality and performance standards

d. Manage contact resolutions for all standard contact types, including escalations from Contact 
Consultants

e. Able to provide pre- and post-sales service and advice to customers across all channels

f. Able to perform all routine administration tasks

g. Can responsibly manage all financial transaction types (purchases and refunds), within delegated 
levels of authority

h. Able to support with documentation of accepted tasks, processes and work types

i. Able to support with general training for Contact Consultants

###### Admin Level 3A – Realtime Support Specialist

258.A team member appointed as a Realtime Support Specialists possess the skills and knowledge of an 
Experienced Consultant or greater, which are applied in management of contact queues and general 
operations planning. This may include, but is not limited to:

a. Maintains detailed knowledge of the contact management systems, and understands response and 
handling performance targets

b. Monitors contact queues and allocates team members to contact channels and queues

c. Communicates between contact centres to support allocation and prioritisation of resourcing d. Allocates resourcing based on requirements for service levels (realtime)

e. Maintain understanding of daily operational focus and goals

f. Communicate performance issues to relevant team leaders for action

g. Communicate regular daily performance updates to senior stakeholders as required

h. Provide regular or ad hoc reporting as required

i. Basic knowledge of Workforce Planning system and schedule adherence

259.A principle feature of this classification is that when not required for queue management tasks, a Realtime 
Support Specialist is able to act as an Experienced Consultant across any contact channel or within the general 
resourcing team.

###### Admin Level 3B – Contact Specialist

their demonstrated experience, training and knowledge of all contact centre systems, technologies, processes 
and enquiry types, with an ability to respond to all issues for which there is no training or documented 
processes.

261.The responsibilities of a Contact Specialist may include, but are not limited to:

a. Ability to handle all contact types for the contact centre, including contacts with complex, sensitive 
or resolution requirements which are not covered by standard operating processes and training

b. Manage financial contact types with higher approval requirements, including general investigations 
or reconciliations for purchases and account entries

c. Contribute to the documentation of contact processes and standards, including review of existing 
processes

d. Able to review the work quality of other team members, including administrative non-contact work

e. Provides training to team members at lower classifications, including realtime feedback and 
coaching, or quality assessments

f. Supervise team members at lower classifications during rostered hours

g. Provide updates on current operational issues in queues which may require support, escalation or 
investigation to remedy

###### Admin Level 4 – Support Specialist

guidance and operational support to the contact centre team members, as well as contributing to overall 
contact centre operational performance, including contact resolutions.

a. Providing general supervision to teams of Consultants and Specialists at lower levels

b. Delivery of structured training, feedback and coaching

c. Manage daily check in / check out procedures for team, including focus priorities and delivery 
requirements

d. Reports on and manages suspected compliance breaches in line with SRG policies and procedures

first aid attendant

f. Acts as a delegated authority on escalated matters

g. Maintains specialised knowledge of workforce planning or quality control processes and standards, 
and is able to support or work directly within those teams

h. May work cross functionally within the contact centre, and contribute to projects or programs of 
work

i. May communicate to other sections of the business, including information or structured 
communications with operational updates

j. Supports with audit, reconciliation and reporting processes

k. Supports in the realtime management of contact centre performance

##### Higher Duties

264.A team member will be performing Higher Duties when a team member is required to temporarily act in a 
position that is at a higher classification.  This will include where a team member is temporarily assigned 
additional responsibilities of a higher classification, including for training and development purposes.

265.Where Higher Duties are worked within a shift, the team member will be paid at the minimum hourly rate
(including penalties) specified in this agreement (see schedule of rates in Appendix A) for the time worked at 
the higher classification.

266.Where Higher Duties are required for an entire shift or longer, payment at the higher classification rate will be 
made for the relevant period as long as it does not exceed 12 consecutive weeks.  Where Higher Duties are 
required to be worked for a period in excess of 12 consecutive weeks, the team member will be placed onto a 
maximum term contract for a specified period, during which they will receive the higher classification rate.

###### Higher Duties for a Supervisor / Shift Supervisor – GRIA Retail Employee Level 3

267.Higher Duties for a Supervisor / Shift Supervisor may arise where the team member is required to temporarily 
act in a Second Level Manager role (being a role mapped to GRIA retail employee level 4) and support the First 
Level Manager to provide leadership, direction and coaching to the store team, including but not limited to:

a. Assisting in the management of the team and day to day operations, inclusive of and up to first level 
performance management

b. Delivery of store budgets, KPIs and operational plans

c. Delivery of operational standards and administrative requirements, including roster generation and 
management

d. Lead, coach and develop store teams

e. Show leadership and take all practicable steps to ensure that the workplace is safe for team and 
customer.

f. Ensure compliance activities are completed and obligations are upheld.

##### Mixed Functions and Mobility

###### Mixed Functions (multiple positions/roles)

268.Team members may undertake a mixture of duties and functions as part of their position / role on a 
temporary or ongoing basis.  Clause 269 provides guidance to support the determination of the relevant 
Agreement (or Award) and classification to apply where multiple classifications may be applicable for the 
variety of duties being undertaken. Clause 269.b refers to duties performed simultaneously or otherwise as a 
single position, for instance during the same shift. Clause 269.c refers to situations where a team member 
holds two distinct positions, typically on separate shifts.

###### 269.As a general rule:

a. SRG will deal with team members at a single instance of employment;

b. team members will be paid in accordance with the classification in this agreement that most 
accurately reflects the tasks that they are performing on a regular basis (typically the part of their 
role that they spend most of their time performing);

c. where a team member performs two positions within SRG, SRG will apply the following principles 
regarding pay for the second position:

i. if the team member is performing work for a second position that attracts a higher pay rate 
under a relevant industrial instrument (whether under this agreement, another enterprise 
agreement or a modern award), then the team member will be paid the higher pay rate for the 
period of time that the work is performed for that second position.

ii. if the team member is performing work for a second position that attracts the same or a lower 
minimum pay rate under a relevant industrial instrument (whether under this agreement, 
another enterprise agreement or a modern award), then the team member will continue to be paid the higher applicable pay rate for their classification level under this agreement for the 
period of time that the work is performed for that second position (see schedule of rates).

###### Mobility

270.Team members may request, or otherwise may mutually agree, to receive scheduled shifts at multiple work 
locations, including across multiple stores, brands or organisational units of SRG.

###### Temporary paid development opportunities

271.SRG is committed to providing development opportunities for team members.  By mutual agreement, such 
development opportunities may include short term (up to 12 consecutive weeks) full-time, part-time or casual 
project work or work placements within support office or other organisational units, brands or locations of 
SRG.  Therefore team members may work across two or more work locations in any week.  Where this occurs 
and for the duration of the development opportunity, team members will remain covered by this Agreement 
and their substantive role, however they will receive a Paid Development Allowance which will reflect the 
percentage difference between their base rate of pay and such higher base rate of pay for the relevant 
classification of the development opportunity (under a modern award, industrial instrument, or 
commensurate with the role).
